question: Do combinations of NautilusTrader's built-in indicators, their parameters and the desk's risk and money management produce a positive net expectancy through BacktestNode?
primary: the money-management axis: does any of reward_floor, a volatility-targeted risk fraction or a volatility gate move net R per trade, against its own duty-cycle twin and against two null arms
secondary: the entry axis: a declared re-measurement of battery.md's family, with the parameters swept, which battery.md did not do
prediction: null on every money-management arm. deriving.md is a theorem that E[net] = -(c/2)*turnover for every stop, target, trail and sizing scheme on a martingale, and geraked-eas.md Mode R measured every risk-layer factor's shift in mean R matching the walks' to within 0.007R.
split_note: discovery is every trade opened before this date, confirmation every trade opened on or after it. Fixed before the run; both halves are reported for every cell that is highlighted.

arm_notes.real: the claim. Four feeds with a recorded DERIV quote to measure a spread from.
arm_notes.walk: each real feed's own log returns resampled i.i.d. with its own bar shapes: the matched null, same instrument, same venue conventions, same measured spread.
arm_notes.synth: Deriv's published-generator indices. Real markets without an auction. Costed to a round trip of 0.063R, the median of the four real legs, because no Deriv synthetic has a recorded quote anywhere in the store - a control's cost, not a tradability claim.

rule_notes.donchian_break: close beyond the PREVIOUS bar's DonchianChannel(n). Previous, because Nautilus updates a registered indicator before on_bar and the current upper is already this bar's high.
rule_notes.rsi_revert: RelativeStrengthIndex(n) crossing back up through 0.30 or down through 0.70.
rule_notes.pairing: every cell is two Nautilus indicators: the signal one above and AverageTrueRange(14), which sets the stop and therefore the risk unit every number is reported in.

base.note: stop 2.0 x ATR(14), target 2.0R, risk 0.25% of equity

floor.note: Profile.floored_target: moves the target out, refuses nothing. Measured by no doc; hold-clock.md names it as the lever.

volsize.note: risk fraction x median(ATR,96)/ATR, clipped to [0.5,2.0]. The sizing-multipliers.md volatility arm on a fresh population; judged on net over risk deployed, which is scale-free, so a multiplier whose mean is not one cannot fake it.

gate.note: trade only where ATR(14) is below its own 96-bar median

twin.note: pass two: keeps signals at random at exactly the keep rate its own gate cell turned out to have

counted.arithmetic: 6 rules x 3 parameters x 4 money-management variants x 4 traded instruments = 288
counted.control_runs: 288 on the walk arm, 288 on the synthetic arm, 72 duty-cycle twins. Controls are not hypotheses and are not in the BH family.
counted.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg over all 288, both tails, never over the survivors.

statistic.primary: mean net R per trade, which is net per unit traded
statistic.net: r_engine minus the entry half-spread the engine does not charge. Measured: at 1.0414 bps and at 100 bps on the same feed the median entry slip was 0.0000100 and 0.0000097, one price increment both times, so bar_execution fills a market order from the bar's own one-tick book and the modelled quote is not the entry price. Stop and target exits are priced off the quote and are left alone.
statistic.error: day-block bootstrap, 2000 draws, resampling whole UTC days, because trades cluster in days and an ordinary standard error is far too narrow
statistic.secondary: sum(pnl)/sum(risk_money) for the sizing arm, which is scale-free; P(reach 2R before the stop) against 1/(1+2) = 0.3333; stop-out share; trades per year

bars.positive: mean net R > 0 with a BH q < 0.05 over 288, positive in BOTH halves, and beating the matched walk cell
bars.money_arm: a money-management variant beats base only if it beats base on net R per trade AND, where it gates, beats its own twin at the same keep rate
bars.null: a clean null is the valued result; power is shown by planting an effect and sweeping its strength
